rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 and Tables 1-3, Figs 6-8 report the authors' own laboratory column experiments on compacted silty sand amended with 5-10% water hyacinth biochar, mesquite biochar and coir pith, measuring SWRC, infiltration rate and crack intensity factor.
rows.notes: The study is a geotechnical laboratory experiment on biochar-amended compacted silty sand (water retention, infiltration rate, desiccation cracking) intended for landfill covers and bioengineered slopes. It contains no drip irrigation, no sprinkler irrigation, no crop, no yield and no water productivity measurement; irrigation is mentioned only as a mariotte-bottle wetting of columns and as a generic remark that higher water retention could reduce irrigation demand. Hence no own evidence on the claimed effect of drip (or sprinkler) on yield or water productivity. The review appears to have mis-cited this study or confused it with another Hussain et al. (2020).

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The cited study is about biochar type effects on soil hydraulic/cracking behaviour of compacted silty sand, not irrigation methods; the claim attributed to it is not supported by anything in the text.
